# Constraint

**Class** · namespace `VRFramework.Interaction.Runtime` · assembly `VRFramework.Interaction.Runtime` · [view source](https://git.cie-group.cz/vr-framework/vrf4/core/-/blob/main/Runtime/Scripts/Interaction/Constraint.cs#L19)

Lets the object turn about one axis, or slide along one, while this grip point is held.

A door, a drawer, a valve, a lever, a bolt. Two of these on one grip point make a power cell:
turn it, then pull it out - and a [`GripSequence`](/api/vrframework-interaction-runtime/GripSequence) holds the pull shut until the
turn is done.

On a grip point when the freedom depends on where the thing is held, and on the grabbable
itself when it does not. A valve with a handle either side of its hub is the second kind: one
of these on the valve, and both handles turn the same one.

```csharp
public class Constraint : GripConstraint
```

### At(Pose, float) {#at-pose-single}

Where a given amount of this constraint's motion puts the object.

A turn is about the pivot rather than about the object's own origin, which is the whole
reason the pivot exists: a door swings about its hinge and the handle travels through an
arc, and taking the origin instead would spin the door on the spot.

```csharp
public Pose At(Pose from, float value)
```

### MoveTo(float) {#moveto-single}

Puts the object at a given point along this travel, whatever a hand is doing.

What a door opened by a script uses, what an author previewing a mechanism uses, and what
a test drives. It writes the object rather than asking for it, so it ignores the hold - a
thing being held will be pulled back by the hand on the next step.
